findings.title: R-024-06 (§7, plan-doc line 208) still describes `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` CI check as 'skips log-entry assertion' — stale framing that contradicts the R3 safety fix applied to invariant 2, §5.2, and §6 024B
findings.evidence: Plan-doc line 208 (§7 risk surface, R-024-06 mitigation column): 'T-024-10 mitigation: cascade slice CLOSES with status blocked-on-adopter-conflict per invariant 10 (forward TF TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> owned by the slice author; new sub-slice opens on conflict resolution). The CI invocation-log check (invariant 2 carve-out) skips log-entry assertion for these close-state slices but verifies the TF reference is present.' The phrase 'skips log-entry assertion for these close-state slices but verifies the TF reference is present' describes a passive check (the CI skip the positive assertion that a log entry exists, and adds one positive TF reference check). This directly contradicts the R3 safety fix applied in fix-round-3 to three other locations: (1) invariant 2 line 47: 'PR MUST NOT modify docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md ... AND MUST reference the filed TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> TF'; (2) §5.2 line 119: 'the PR MUST NOT modify branch-protection-log.md (CI script asserts absence of modification per invariant 2)'; (3) §6 024B acceptance row line 190: 'for blocked-on-adopter-conflict: requires TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> reference AND asserts log file was NOT modified (closes the R3 safety bypass)'. The R3 safety finding (FIX-ROUND-3.md R3-NEW-MAJ-001 safety) was precisely that the prior version of invariant 2 only required positive evidence (TF reference present) but did NOT require negative evidence (log NOT modified). R-024-06 still describes the old pre-R3 posture: one positive check ('verifies the TF reference is present'), no negative assertion. The R3 safety fix added the second requirement: the CI MUST assert log file was NOT modified. R-024-06 omits this second requirement entirely. R-024-06 is normative governance text — it is the risk-surface summary that a future cascade slice author (024C–024F) reads to understand what the CI gate enforces for conflict-close slices. The stale 'skips log-entry assertion' framing could cause a slice author to believe a passive omission satisfies the CI gate, which would reopen the bypass surface that R3 safety closed.
findings.recommendation: Update plan-doc §7 R-024-06 mitigation column (line 208) to replace 'The CI invocation-log check (invariant 2 carve-out) skips log-entry assertion for these close-state slices but verifies the TF reference is present.' with 'The CI enforcement script (024B) applies the blocked-on-adopter-conflict check-path per invariant 2: the PR MUST NOT modify docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md (CI asserts absence of modification — no invocation occurred) AND MUST reference the filed TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> in DISPATCH-NOTE. (Closes 024A R3 R3-NEW-MAJ-001 safety — earlier text described only the positive TF check, omitting the negative log-file assertion.)'
